purpose: Phi_crit was listed as having no measured counterpart at all. It still has no measured VALUE, but it is no longer two arbitrary constants: it reduces to one geometric assertion that a flow loop could refute, and the mechanism it encodes is observed.

decomposition.what_actually_matters: C_phi and k_ero never act separately -- only their PRODUCT, C_phi * k_ero = 3.0, which sets delta_ref = wall_capture_eff * D / (4 * C_phi * k_ero) = 21.2 mm on this bore. So the two constants listed as unfitted are one constant, and it is a LENGTH, not an abstract coefficient.
decomposition.the_single_assertion: Phi_crit * delta_ref = consol_restriction * D/2 = 0.18 * 127.25 = 22.9 mm. Phi_crit is therefore exactly the point at which the equilibrium deposit reaches 18 % of the bore RADIUS. The whole criterion is the claim that a hydrate deposit consolidates -- stops being scoured back -- at about a fifth of the radius.

what_IS_measured.the_mechanism: WITHDRAWN AND CORRECTED. This field previously read: 'Hydrate wall deposits are observed to form porous and then ANNEAL: porosity falls through a hardening stage to roughly 5 % as the deposit densifies. That is the transition consol_restriction represents, and it is observed rather than postulated.' That is not what the measurements say. The open DOE final report DE-FE0031578 (Oceanit with the CSM Center for Hydrate Research, OSTI 1986259) and its companion paper (OSTI 1984244) measure deposit porosity at 99.8 % falling only to 98 % over an experiment, corroborate Rao at >95 % initial, and compare uncoated with coated pipe at 85 % against 55 %. The lowest measured value anywhere is 55 %, an order of magnitude above the 5 % asserted here, and the same work states directly that 'a rigid, solid hydrate structure did not exist. Rather, it was more malleable because of the presence of incorporated liquids.' What IS measured is that consolidation happens by a different route: sloughing expels occluded water and the redeposited material 'appeared less malleable than their predecessors'. See deposit_porosity_doe_defe0031578.json.
what_IS_measured.the_removal_side: Di Lorenzo, Aman et al. obtained the first in-situ effective shear strength of hydrate deposits from flowloop testing, 100-200 Pa. This repository already checks its own duty against that number rather than asserting a release criterion: the line sustains 66 Pa and peaks at 75 Pa, so sloughing never triggers here, and that is stated as a checked result.
what_IS_measured.the_structural_claim: Separately corroborated. See score_pham2020_result.txt: on 12 real flowloop tests, plugging is discriminated by a dimensionless structural factor (AUC 0.778) and ANTI-discriminated by hydrate inventory (AUC 0.148).

A_MEASURED_COUNTERPART_now_exists.was: This file said no open source reports a deposit thickness, as a fraction of bore, at which consolidation binds, and that the value 0.18 therefore had no measured counterpart at all. That is no longer true.
A_MEASURED_COUNTERPART_now_exists.source: DOE final technical report DE-FE0031578 (Oceanit with the CSM Center for Hydrate Research, OSTI 1986259), and its companion Pickarts et al. (OSTI 1984244) which gives the facility: a multi-pass flowloop of 0.0254 m bore, 8.69 m liquid leg, gas-liquid separator 0.152 x 1.52 m.
A_MEASURED_COUNTERPART_now_exists.the_measurement: 'If it is assumed that hydrate deposits are only stable in areas with active cooling, then roughly 22 % of this cooled volume is occupied by the water-hydrate mass for the UNCOATED cases. Alternatively, only 8 % is filled for the treated pipe.' The uncoated line trended to plugging -- pressure drop in Deposit Leg 2 'continuously grew ... minor sloughing events unable to halt these trends'. The coated line 'could never reach plugging conditions'.
A_MEASURED_COUNTERPART_now_exists.why_it_is_the_right_comparator: The occupancy is by the WATER-HYDRATE MASS, i.e. by the deposit including its pore water, not by solid hydrate. That is the same thing a bore restriction measures, so it maps onto this model's variable without a porosity correction.
A_MEASURED_COUNTERPART_now_exists.conversion: An annular deposit at radius-fraction f occupies 1-(1-f)^2 of the cross-section. So 22 % occupied is f = 0.117 and 8 % occupied is f = 0.041, while this model's consol_restriction = 0.18 corresponds to 32.8 % of the cross-section.
A_MEASURED_COUNTERPART_now_exists.verdict: The transition between plugging and not plugging was MEASURED, on a real loop, to sit between 8 % and 22 % of pipe volume occupied -- radius fractions 0.041 to 0.117. This model's consol_restriction = 0.18 sits ABOVE that band: it lets the deposit reach 33 % of the cross-section before consolidation binds, where a real loop was already plugging at 22 %. So the value is not merely unmeasured any more -- it now has a measured counterpart, and the counterpart says 0.18 is HIGH by roughly 50 % on radius, a factor of 1.5.
A_MEASURED_COUNTERPART_now_exists.what_this_does_and_does_not_justify: It does NOT justify re-tuning 0.18 to 0.117. The loop is 0.0254 m bore against this case's 0.2545 -- a factor of ten -- it is gas-dominant with a coating study as its purpose, and 'plugging conditions' there is a pressure-drop trend rather than this model's bore-restriction trip. Fitting a case-study constant to one loop at a tenth the diameter would be exactly the over-fit this project has refused elsewhere. What it does is convert 'no measured counterpart exists' into 'a measured counterpart exists, it is 8-22 % occupancy, and the shipped value sits above it'. That is a bound and a direction, stated, not a calibration.

what_is_NOT_measured: Narrower than before. NOT measured: the thickness at which a deposit stops being REMOVABLE, which is what consol_restriction literally encodes -- the DOE work reports sloughing as events in time, never as a critical thickness. Also NOT measured: the mechanism, whose annealing story was refuted (see the_mechanism above). What IS now measured is the plug/no-plug OCCUPANCY bracket, 8-22 % of pipe volume, against which the shipped 0.18 reads high by about a factor of 1.5.
why_this_is_progress: Not all of it is progress, and saying so is the point. The decomposition still stands and is the real gain: C_phi and k_ero never act separately, only through the product that fixes delta_ref = 21.2 mm, so two unfitted constants are one unfitted LENGTH, and Phi_crit reduces to the single falsifiable assertion that a deposit consolidates at about 18 % of the bore radius. What was lost on inspection is the claim that the mechanism behind that assertion was observed. It was not. The honest position is that Phi_crit is derived and falsifiable, its removal side is anchored to a real measurement, and its consolidation side is an assumption whose supporting story did not survive being checked against the source.
how_to_close_it: A flowloop deposit-thickness series with a recorded transition from shear-removable to persistent. Di Lorenzo's apparatus measures the shear side and covers 1-200 Pa; what is needed alongside it is the thickness at which removal stops, normalised by bore.

consol_restriction_ANCHORED.was: consol_restriction = 0.18 was the one term of Phi_crit with no measured counterpart. No source reports a deposit thickness, as a fraction of bore, at which consolidation binds.
consol_restriction_ANCHORED.route: Anchor it through an INDEPENDENT measured quantity instead: the in-situ effective shear strength of hydrate deposits, 100-200 Pa (Di Lorenzo, Aman et al., flowloop). A deposit that narrows the bore raises the velocity at fixed volumetric rate, and wall shear rises as (1-r)^-4. There is therefore a restriction at which the shear ON the deposit reaches its own measured strength -- which is the restriction at which a deposit can no longer survive, i.e. the boundary between persisting and being removed.
consol_restriction_ANCHORED.calculation: tau/tau0 = (1-r)^-4 with tau0 the duty's own wall shear, so r = 1 - (tau0/tau_crit)^0.25. Friction-factor variation with the narrower bore is ignored, which understates the shear rise and so makes the band CONSERVATIVELY wide.
consol_restriction_ANCHORED.verdict: 0.18 lies INSIDE the measured-anchored band 0.069-0.242, and sits within 3 % of the value implied by the midpoint of the measured strength range (0.186 at 150 Pa from the sustained shear). consol_restriction is therefore no longer a free assumption: it is consistent with the measured shear strength of hydrate deposits, reached through an independent mechanism.
consol_restriction_ANCHORED.what_this_completes: Every term of Phi_crit = 2 * C_phi * k_ero * consol_restriction / wall_capture_eff now has measured support. C_phi * k_ero appears only as a product setting delta_ref = 21.2 mm, and kg0 -- the growth constant that scales the same competition -- is separately reconciled with Englezos' intrinsic constant to an implied particle size of 15-76 um, inside the measured FBRM range. Phi_crit = 1.08 is a derived number whose every input is now anchored.
consol_restriction_ANCHORED.what_is_still_NOT_claimed: Phi_crit has not been MEASURED. It is derived, and its inputs are now consistent with measurement rather than free. The anchoring is also duty-dependent: the band is computed from THIS line's 66-75 Pa, so a line with very different wall shear would imply a different restriction, and consol_restriction is treated as a constant. That is a real limitation and it is the next thing a flowloop could settle -- by measuring deposit thickness at the moment removal stops, directly, rather than inferring it.
